html:
Between 1967 and 1973 Britain removed the whole population of the Chagos Islands, about 1,500 people, to Mauritius and the Seychelles, to make way for a United States military base on Diego Garcia.

In 1965, before independence, Britain had split the islands from Mauritius to form the British Indian Ocean Territory. The Chagossians, descendants of enslaved Africans and Indian workers on coconut plantations, were shipped off with little help and lived in poverty in Port Louis.

They fought for decades in British courts to go home. In 2019 the International Court of Justice advised that Britain should hand the islands to Mauritius, and in 2025 Britain signed a treaty to do so while keeping the base on Diego Garcia. It recalls Mauritian anger at the deal made under Ramgoolam.
sum: Between 1967 and 1973 Britain removed the whole population of the Chagos Islands, about 1,500 people, to Mauritius and the Seychelles, to make way for a United States military base on Diego Garcia.
